intent.raw_query: Morocco Marrakech and Sahara, $1000 solo, 7 days, March 2026

experiences.name: Djemaa el-Fna Square Evening Immersion
experiences.description: Skip Day 1 evening exhaustion by staying near the Medina. On Day 2 morning, explore the iconic Djemaa el-Fna square when it is less crowded, then return at dusk for storytellers, snake charmers, and street food stalls. Staying at a riad within walking distance of the square eliminates transfer time and maximizes your first full day. Budget for fresh orange juice, street snacks, and a guided 1-hour orientation walk.

experiences.name: Saadian Tombs and El Badi Palace Half-Day History Walk
experiences.description: Both 16th-century sites are within a 10-minute walk of each other in the southern Medina, making them ideal for a combined morning visit before midday heat. The Saadian Tombs reveal intricate Moroccan craftsmanship, while El Badi Palace offers sweeping views from its ramparts. Staying in a Kasbah-area riad puts you steps away, avoiding costly taxis and wasted travel time flagged by the coordinator.

experiences.name: Marrakech Souks and Traditional Craft Workshop
experiences.description: Navigate the labyrinthine souks of the northern Medina and join a 2-hour hands-on workshop in a local tannery or pottery cooperative. This experience is best done mid-morning before tour groups arrive. Choosing accommodation in the Mouassine or Bab Doukkala neighborhood keeps you within a 5-minute walk of the souk entrances, directly addressing the coordinator's concern about activity proximity.
experiences.location: Souk Semmarine and Mouassine quarter, northern Medina, Marrakech

experiences.name: Sahara Desert Overnight Camel Trek and Stargazing Camp
experiences.description: Depart Marrakech on Day 3 via shared transfer to Merzouga (or take a pre-booked private 4x4 to save time). Ride camels into the Erg Chebbi dunes at sunset, spend the night in a traditional Berber camp with live music and a guided stargazing session, then witness sunrise over the dunes before returning. Book a camp operator based in Merzouga village to eliminate extra transfers within the desert region, directly addressing the coordinator's proximity concern.
experiences.location: Erg Chebbi dunes, Merzouga, Sahara Desert

experiences.name: Atlas Mountains Day Hike via Imlil Village
experiences.description: On Day 6, join a small-group guided hike from Imlil village through Berber hamlets and terraced valleys toward the Toubkal foothills. The trailhead is 90 minutes from Marrakech, so an early 07:00 departure is essential — book accommodation near Bab Agnaou or hire a driver the night before to avoid morning delays. This adventure-history hybrid reveals traditional Amazigh culture and dramatic mountain scenery within your budget.
experiences.location: Imlil village, High Atlas Mountains, Marrakech Province

trip_options.title: Budget Explorer - Morocco (Marrakech and Sahara)
trip_options.description: Save money without sacrificing the experience. Perfect for travelers who value authentic local experiences over luxury.

day_by_day.morning: Arrival at Marrakech Menara Airport at 13:00 — no morning activities scheduled. Take a petit taxi (negotiate fare, ~50-70 MAD) or shared airport bus to your riad in the Medina district. Check in, freshen up, and get oriented.
day_by_day.afternoon: Gentle first explore: Stroll through Djemaa el-Fna square to absorb the atmosphere — snake charmers, storytellers, and street performers. Walk into the nearby souks (Souk Semmarine) to get your bearings without buying yet. Visit the free exterior of Koutoubia Mosque and its gardens for a relaxed sit-down.
day_by_day.evening: Return to Djemaa el-Fna as it transforms at sunset — the square fills with food stalls, musicians, and acrobats. Grab a front-row seat at one of the rooftop terraces overlooking the square for mint tea (~15 MAD) and soak in the spectacle.

meals.breakfast: Eat on the plane or grab a quick snack from a Medina bakery near your riad on arrival (msemen flatbread or a khobz roll with amlou, ~10-15 MAD)
meals.lunch: Street food at Djemaa el-Fna — harira soup (10 MAD), a kefta sandwich (20 MAD), or fresh-squeezed orange juice (4 MAD per glass)
meals.dinner: Djemaa el-Fna night food stalls — choose stall #1-#100 area for grilled merguez, brochettes, and salads. Full meal ~50-70 MAD. Tip: stalls with the most locals are the best quality.

day_by_day.notes: Day 1 is intentionally light — jet lag and orientation are the priority. Exchange some cash at the airport or a Medina bureau de change (avoid hotels). Keep small change (1-5 MAD coins) handy for tips. Confirm with your riad if check-in before 14:00 is possible.

day_by_day.morning: Historic Medina deep dive: Visit the Bahia Palace (entrance ~70 MAD) — a stunning 19th-century vizier's palace with ornate tilework and carved cedar ceilings. Then walk 5 minutes to the Mellah (Jewish quarter) and explore its covered market and old synagogue (free to wander exterior).
day_by_day.afternoon: Head to the Ben Youssef Madrasa (entrance ~70 MAD), one of the most beautifully decorated Islamic schools in North Africa. Afterward, explore the surrounding souks by craft type: Souk des Teinturiers (dyers' souk) and Souk Cherratine (leather workers). Bargaining is expected — start at 40% of asking price.
day_by_day.evening: Visit the rooftop of a souk-area café for sunset views over the Medina rooftops. Explore the quieter northern Medina alleys near Bab Doukkala gate as evening falls — far fewer tourists and very atmospheric.

meals.breakfast: At your riad (often included) or a local café near the Medina — café au lait, msemen with honey and argan oil, ~20-30 MAD
meals.lunch: Snack lunch in the souks — a fresh khobz sandwich with kefta from a hole-in-the-wall grill (~25 MAD) and a glass of fresh-squeezed orange juice (~4 MAD)
meals.dinner: Restaurant Souk Kafe or similar budget Medina restaurant — tagine with bread ~60-80 MAD. Look for set menus (menu du jour) for best value.

day_by_day.notes: Wear comfortable walking shoes — Medina streets are uneven cobblestones. The Ben Youssef Madrasa can get crowded by 10:00 AM; aim to arrive right at opening (9:00 AM). Carry a small daypack and keep valuables in a front pocket.

day_by_day.morning: Saadian Tombs (entrance ~70 MAD) — 16th-century royal necropolis rediscovered in 1917, featuring intricate marble and mosaic work. Then walk to El Badi Palace ruins (entrance ~70 MAD) — a vast 16th-century palace complex, now a dramatic open-air ruin with resident storks nesting on the walls.
day_by_day.afternoon: Explore the Kasbah neighbourhood and Mellah market for local produce and spices. Visit a free argan oil cooperative workshop (many offer free demonstrations — no obligation to buy, though prices are fair at source). Walk along the ancient Medina ramparts near Bab Agnaou gate.
day_by_day.evening: Hammam experience — visit a traditional local hammam (not a tourist spa). Hammam Mouassine or a neighbourhood hammam costs ~20-50 MAD for a basic scrub session. This is a deeply authentic cultural experience and very budget-friendly.

meals.breakfast: Riad breakfast or street-side café — amlou (almond-argan dip) with khobz, mint tea, ~25 MAD
meals.lunch: Lunch at a Mellah market stall — bissara (fava bean soup with olive oil and cumin, ~15 MAD) and bread, a classic Moroccan working-class lunch
meals.dinner: Cook-your-own option: buy fresh produce, olives, cheese, and bread from Mellah market (~40-50 MAD total) and have a picnic-style dinner at your riad or rooftop terrace

day_by_day.notes: Combine the Saadian Tombs and El Badi Palace into one morning loop — they are only 5 minutes apart on foot. The hammam is best experienced in the late afternoon/early evening when locals use it. Ask your riad host to recommend the nearest authentic neighbourhood hammam.

day_by_day.morning: Day trip to the Ourika Valley (Atlas Mountains foothills, ~30 km from Marrakech). Take a shared grand taxi from Bab Rob gate (~30-40 MAD per person each way). Hike along the Ourika River through Berber villages to the Setti Fatma waterfalls (1-2 hour walk each way, free entry to valley).
day_by_day.afternoon: Explore Setti Fatma village — visit a local Berber family's home for mint tea if invited (a common and genuine gesture of hospitality, ~10-20 MAD tip appreciated). Begin the return journey to Marrakech by shared taxi. Arrive back in the Medina by late afternoon.
day_by_day.evening: Relax evening in Djemaa el-Fna — watch the Gnawa musicians and storytellers. Browse the evening souk stalls for souvenirs (best prices after 19:00 when vendors want to close sales).

meals.breakfast: Early riad breakfast before departure — essential to fuel the hike
meals.lunch: Riverside Berber restaurant in Ourika Valley — tagine and salad with bread ~60-80 MAD. Sit on a terrace directly over the river for the full experience.
meals.dinner: Djemaa el-Fna food stalls or a cheap Medina restaurant — merguez sandwich and harira ~40-50 MAD

day_by_day.notes: Start early (depart by 8:00 AM) to avoid midday heat on the hike and to get the best shared taxi prices. Bring water (2L per person), sunscreen, and sturdy shoes. March weather in the Atlas foothills can be cool — bring a light layer. The waterfalls may have variable flow depending on winter snowmelt.

day_by_day.morning: Depart Marrakech early for the Sahara Desert (Merzouga/Erg Chebbi). Take a shared CTM bus or a budget shared minivan transfer (~150-200 MAD, book 1-2 days ahead via your riad). The journey is ~9-10 hours through the High Atlas via Tizi n'Tichka pass and Draa Valley — the drive itself is spectacular. Pass through Ouarzazate (the 'Hollywood of Africa') around midday.
day_by_day.afternoon: Continue through the Draa Valley oasis towns — Agdz, Zagora — watching the landscape shift from mountains to desert kasbahs and palm oases. Arrive in Merzouga (gateway to Erg Chebbi dunes) in the late afternoon. Check into a budget desert camp or guesthouse (~150-200 MAD/night for a basic room).
day_by_day.evening: Camel trek into the Erg Chebbi dunes at sunset (~100-150 MAD for a 1-hour guided sunset trek). Watch the sun sink behind the dunes, turning the sand gold and orange. Return to camp for a Berber drum circle and traditional dinner under the stars.

meals.breakfast: Early riad breakfast before bus departure — pack extra snacks for the road
meals.lunch: Roadside stop in Ouarzazate — tagine or sandwich at a local café ~40-60 MAD. The bus/minivan typically makes a 30-minute lunch stop.
meals.dinner: Included in most budget desert camp packages — traditional Berber couscous or tagine, mint tea, and bread around a communal fire (~included or ~80 MAD if separate)

day_by_day.notes: Book your Sahara transport and accommodation at least 2 days in advance through your Marrakech riad — they often have reliable contacts and can negotiate fair prices. Pack a warm layer: desert nights in March can drop to 5-10°C. A shared minivan is more flexible than the bus and allows scenic stops. Bring cash — ATMs are scarce beyond Ouarzazate.

day_by_day.morning: Wake before sunrise (around 6:00 AM) for a dawn camel ride or walk to the top of the highest dune at Erg Chebbi — the sunrise over the Sahara is one of Morocco's most iconic experiences. Spend the morning sandboarding down the dunes (boards often available at camp for free or ~20 MAD rental) and exploring the desert on foot.
day_by_day.afternoon: Visit the village of Merzouga and the nearby Dayet Srji salt lake (seasonal — may have flamingos in spring). Explore a local fossil and mineral shop (the Merzouga area is rich in Devonian-era fossils — good budget souvenirs). Rest during the hottest part of the afternoon at your guesthouse.
day_by_day.evening: Optional second sunset in the dunes (free if you walk yourself) or relax at the guesthouse rooftop. Enjoy a final Sahara night — the star-gazing here, with zero light pollution, is extraordinary. Berber tea ceremony with your hosts.

meals.breakfast: Guesthouse breakfast — khobz, olive oil, honey, hard-boiled eggs, and mint tea (~included or ~30 MAD)
meals.lunch: Guesthouse or local Merzouga café — tagine or omelette with bread ~50-60 MAD
meals.dinner: Guesthouse dinner — many offer a set Berber dinner (couscous on Saturdays is traditional in Morocco) ~80-100 MAD or negotiate a full-board rate when booking

day_by_day.notes: March is an excellent time for the Sahara — not yet scorching hot (daytime ~25-28°C) but warm enough to enjoy. Protect your camera and phone from fine sand. The Erg Chebbi dunes rise to 150m — the climb is tiring in soft sand but very rewarding. Negotiate fossil prices — start at 50% of asking price.

day_by_day.morning: Depart Merzouga early (6:00-7:00 AM) for the return journey to Marrakech via shared minivan/CTM bus (~150-200 MAD). Enjoy the reverse journey through the Draa Valley and over the High Atlas — consider stopping briefly in Ouarzazate to see the exterior of the Atlas Film Studios (the largest film studios in the world by area — Mad Max, Gladiator, Game of Thrones were filmed here; exterior view is free, tours ~50 MAD).
day_by_day.afternoon: Arrive back in Marrakech by late afternoon (~17:00-18:00). Return to your Medina riad, shower, and decompress. Final souk shopping for last-minute gifts — leather goods, argan products, spices, and Berber textiles are all excellent value in Marrakech.
day_by_day.evening: Final evening in Djemaa el-Fna — a farewell lap of the square, one last glass of fresh orange juice, and a final tagine dinner. Reflect on the week over mint tea on a rooftop terrace overlooking the floodlit Koutoubia Mosque.

meals.breakfast: Guesthouse breakfast in Merzouga before departure — pack snacks for the road
meals.lunch: Roadside stop en route — sandwich or harira soup at a local café ~30-40 MAD
meals.dinner: Splurge slightly for your last night — a sit-down Medina restaurant with a proper set menu: harira, pastilla (pigeon pie), lamb tagine, and mint tea ~100-120 MAD — still very budget-friendly by any standard

day_by_day.notes: Confirm your return transport the evening before departure in Merzouga. If your flight home is the next day, ask your riad about late checkout or luggage storage. Budget summary for 7 days (approximate per person): Accommodation ~900-1200 MAD, Transport ~500-700 MAD, Food ~700-900 MAD, Entrance fees ~350-400 MAD, Activities ~300-400 MAD — Total approximately 2750-3700 MAD (~$275-370 USD). Morocco is genuinely one of the world's best budget travel destinations.

trip_options.title: Classic Morocco (Marrakech and Sahara) Experience
trip_options.description: The sweet spot between comfort and value. Enjoy quality accommodations, diverse experiences, and good food.

day_by_day.morning: Arrival at Marrakech Menara Airport at 13:00 — no morning activities scheduled. Transfer to your boutique riad in the Medina district (~30 min by taxi, ~150 MAD). Check in, freshen up, and settle into your accommodation.
day_by_day.afternoon: Take a gentle orientation stroll through the nearby souks of the Medina. Wander through Souk Semmarine and Souk des Épices to get your bearings, absorb the sights, sounds, and aromas, and pick up a hand-drawn map from your riad host. Visit the Bahia Palace (entry ~70 MAD) if energy allows — it's a 10-minute walk from most Medina riads.
day_by_day.evening: Head to Djemaa el-Fna square as the sun sets to witness the famous transformation: snake charmers, storytellers, musicians, and dozens of food stalls lighting up. Enjoy the spectacle from a rooftop café terrace overlooking the square.

meals.breakfast: Skipped / light snack on the plane
meals.lunch: Grab a quick bite near the airport or at a café in the Medina upon arrival — try a fresh msemen (flatbread) with argan honey at a local bakery (~30–50 MAD)
meals.dinner: Dinner at one of the Djemaa el-Fna food stalls — try harira soup, merguez brochettes, and kefta tagine cooked fresh on open grills (~80–120 MAD per person)

day_by_day.notes: Carry small change (MAD) for tips and stall purchases. Agree on taxi fare before entering the cab from the airport. Your riad host can provide a neighborhood map and safety tips. March evenings in Marrakech are mild (~15°C), bring a light jacket.

day_by_day.morning: Start with a traditional Moroccan breakfast at your riad (often included — mint tea, msemen, amlou, fresh orange juice). Then visit the Koutoubia Mosque gardens for a peaceful morning walk and photography (non-Muslims admire from outside). Head to the Saadian Tombs (entry ~70 MAD) — a stunning 16th-century royal necropolis just 10 minutes from the Koutoubia.
day_by_day.afternoon: Explore the El Badi Palace ruins (entry ~70 MAD), a sprawling 16th-century palace complex with storks nesting on the walls and panoramic views from the ramparts. Afterward, visit the Mellah (Jewish Quarter) nearby to explore its distinctive architecture, covered market, and the historic Lazama Synagogue (free entry, donation welcome).
day_by_day.evening: Take a cooking class at a local culinary school or riad kitchen (typically 350–500 MAD per person, bookable through your riad). Learn to make a classic chicken tagine with preserved lemon and olives, plus Moroccan salads. Enjoy the meal you've prepared as dinner.

meals.breakfast: At your riad — traditional Moroccan spread with mint tea, bread, olive oil, and honey
meals.lunch: Lunch at Café Clock in the Kasbah area (~100–150 MAD) — known for its camel burger and traditional Moroccan dishes in a relaxed courtyard setting
meals.dinner: Dinner from your cooking class experience, or dine at a mid-range restaurant like Le Jardin in the Medina (~150–200 MAD per person)

day_by_day.notes: Book the cooking class in advance through your riad or online. The Saadian Tombs can get crowded mid-morning — arrive by 9:00 AM for a quieter experience. Comfortable walking shoes are essential for cobblestone streets.

day_by_day.morning: Day trip to the Atlas Mountains and Ourika Valley (~30 km south of Marrakech). Hire a shared grand taxi or join a small group tour (~200–300 MAD per person). Drive through Berber villages, terraced fields, and dramatic mountain scenery. Visit a local Berber family home for mint tea and a glimpse of traditional mountain life.
day_by_day.afternoon: Continue to the Ourika Valley waterfalls — hike up the rocky trail (moderate, ~45 min each way) to reach the cascades surrounded by lush greenery. The views of the High Atlas are spectacular in March when snow still caps the peaks. Return to Marrakech by late afternoon.
day_by_day.evening: Relax and explore the northern Medina — visit the Ben Youssef Madrasa (entry ~70 MAD, one of North Africa's most beautiful Islamic schools, though check restoration status) and the adjacent Marrakech Museum housed in the Dar Menebhi Palace (~50 MAD). End the evening with a hammam experience at a traditional public hammam or a mid-range riad hammam (~150–300 MAD).

meals.breakfast: At your riad before departure
meals.lunch: Lunch at a riverside restaurant in the Ourika Valley — fresh trout from the river, Moroccan salads, and bread (~100–150 MAD per person)
meals.dinner: Dinner at a rooftop restaurant in the Medina — try Nomad restaurant for modern Moroccan cuisine with stunning Medina views (~180–250 MAD per person)

day_by_day.notes: Arrange the Atlas day trip through your riad the evening before for the best price. Wear layers — the mountains are noticeably cooler than Marrakech in March. Bring sunscreen and water for the waterfall hike. The hammam is a must-try cultural experience — your riad can recommend a reputable one.

day_by_day.morning: Depart early (6:00–7:00 AM) for the Sahara Desert — a long but spectacular drive (~8–9 hours) through the High Atlas via the Tizi n'Tichka pass (2,260m), the ancient kasbah town of Ait Ben Haddou (UNESCO World Heritage Site), and the dramatic Draa Valley. Travel by private driver or shared tour (~500–700 MAD per person for a 3-day desert tour package).
day_by_day.afternoon: Stop at Ait Ben Haddou for a guided walk through the ancient fortified ksar (entry ~10 MAD). Climb to the top granary for panoramic views of the surrounding desert landscape. This UNESCO site has featured in films like Gladiator and Game of Thrones. Continue driving through Ouarzazate (the 'Hollywood of Africa') — optional stop at the Atlas Film Studios (~50 MAD entry).
day_by_day.evening: Arrive in the Draa Valley or Agdz area by early evening. Check into a mid-range kasbah guesthouse (~400–600 MAD/night). Enjoy a traditional Berber dinner under a sky full of stars on the terrace, with live Gnawa music if available.

meals.breakfast: Early breakfast at your riad before departure — or grab coffee and msemen at a roadside café en route
meals.lunch: Lunch stop in Ait Ben Haddou or a roadside restaurant near the Tizi n'Tichka pass (~80–120 MAD) — try a lamb tagine with prunes and almonds
meals.dinner: Dinner at your kasbah guesthouse — included in most desert tour packages; expect harira, tagine, couscous, and fresh fruit (~included or ~150 MAD)

day_by_day.notes: This is a long driving day — start as early as possible. The Tizi n'Tichka pass is stunning but winding; those prone to motion sickness should take precautions. A private driver gives more flexibility for stops. Confirm your accommodation booking in advance as options are limited in remote areas.

day_by_day.morning: Continue driving east through the Draa Valley palm groves toward Merzouga and the Erg Chebbi dunes (~4–5 hours). Stop at the rose-growing town of Kelaat M'Gouna if passing through in rose season (March is early but blooms may be starting). Arrive at Merzouga village by midday.
day_by_day.afternoon: Check into a mid-range desert camp or guesthouse on the edge of the dunes (~500–800 MAD including camel ride and dinner). Rest during the hottest part of the afternoon. At around 4:00–5:00 PM, mount camels for a guided dromedary trek into the Erg Chebbi dunes — the largest sand dunes in Morocco, reaching up to 150 meters. Ride to your overnight desert camp as the sun begins to lower.
day_by_day.evening: Watch the spectacular Sahara sunset from the top of a sand dune — the colors shift from gold to deep orange to purple. Arrive at your desert camp (traditional Berber tents with basic but comfortable bedding). Enjoy a campfire dinner with Berber musicians playing traditional desert music. Sleep under an extraordinary canopy of stars with zero light pollution.

meals.breakfast: Breakfast at your kasbah guesthouse before departure
meals.lunch: Lunch in Merzouga village upon arrival — a simple local restaurant serving tagine and fresh bread (~80–100 MAD)
meals.dinner: Traditional Berber camp dinner included in your desert package — typically lamb or vegetable tagine, couscous, Moroccan salads, and mint tea around the campfire

day_by_day.notes: Bring a headscarf or buff to protect against sand during the camel trek. March nights in the Sahara can drop to 5–10°C — pack a warm layer. Charge all devices before heading into the dunes (no electricity in most traditional camps). Sunrise from the dunes the following morning is unmissable — set your alarm for 5:30 AM.

day_by_day.morning: Wake before sunrise (~5:30 AM) to climb the nearest high dune for a breathtaking Sahara sunrise — one of the most memorable experiences of the trip. Return to camp for a simple breakfast. Take a final walk through the dunes before camel trekking back to Merzouga village. Freshen up at your guesthouse and begin the long return journey to Marrakech via a different route through the Ziz Valley and Errachidia.
day_by_day.afternoon: Drive through the stunning Ziz Gorges and the vast Ziz palm grove oasis — one of Morocco's most dramatic landscapes. Stop at the Source Bleue de Meski, a natural spring oasis surrounded by palms, for a short break and photos. Continue through Midelt and the cedar forests of the Middle Atlas, where Barbary macaques may be spotted.
day_by_day.evening: Arrive back in Marrakech by late evening (~9:00–10:00 PM after a full driving day). Check back into your Medina riad. Freshen up and have a late dinner near the riad.

meals.breakfast: Simple camp breakfast — bread, jam, mint tea, and fresh fruit
meals.lunch: Roadside lunch stop in Errachidia or Midelt (~80–120 MAD) — try a hearty lamb or chicken tagine to fuel the long drive
meals.dinner: Late dinner near your riad — try a small local restaurant in the Medina for a simple but satisfying kefta tagine or pastilla (~100–150 MAD)

day_by_day.notes: This is another long driving day (~9–10 hours with stops). Sleep in the car when possible. The Ziz Valley route offers completely different scenery from the outward journey — worth the extra time. Confirm with your driver the exact return route and expected arrival time. Hydrate well throughout the day.

day_by_day.morning: Final morning in Marrakech — spend it leisurely exploring any remaining Medina highlights. Visit the vibrant Mellah spice market for aromatic souvenirs (saffron, ras el hanout, argan oil). Browse the artisan souks for last-minute gifts — the leather souk (tanneries are a short walk north), carpet souk, and lantern souk are all within the Medina. Practice your bargaining skills for authentic Moroccan crafts.
day_by_day.afternoon: Visit the Majorelle Garden (entry ~150 MAD, or ~200 MAD including the Berber Museum inside) — a stunning botanical garden created by French painter Jacques Majorelle and later owned by Yves Saint Laurent. The electric blue villa and exotic plants make it one of Marrakech's most photogenic spots. Afterward, visit the nearby Yves Saint Laurent Museum (~100 MAD) for a fascinating look at fashion history intertwined with Morocco.
day_by_day.evening: Final farewell dinner at a mid-range traditional Moroccan restaurant in the Medina — splurge slightly for your last night. Consider a restaurant with live traditional music. Afterward, take one last stroll through Djemaa el-Fna to soak in the atmosphere before heading back to your riad to pack for departure.

meals.breakfast: Final riad breakfast — savor the mint tea, msemen, and amlou one last time
meals.lunch: Lunch at a café near the Majorelle Garden — Café Bousafsaf or a similar garden café (~120–160 MAD) for salads, sandwiches, and fresh juices
meals.dinner: Farewell dinner at Dar Yacout or a similar mid-to-upper mid-range traditional riad restaurant (~250–350 MAD per person) — enjoy a full Moroccan feast with pastilla, tagine, couscous, and bastilla au lait for dessert

day_by_day.notes: Book the Majorelle Garden tickets online in advance — it's one of Marrakech's most popular attractions and can sell out, especially on weekends. Arrange your airport transfer the night before (taxi ~150 MAD or pre-booked transfer ~250 MAD). Keep some MAD for tips and last-minute purchases. The Marrakech Medina is a UNESCO World Heritage Site — take time on your last evening to simply sit, observe, and appreciate the living history around you.

highlights: Mix of paid and free experiences

trip_options.title: Premium Morocco (Marrakech and Sahara) Escape
trip_options.description: Indulge in the best the destination has to offer. Premium flights, luxury hotels, and exclusive experiences.

day_by_day.morning: Arrival at Marrakech Menara Airport at 13:00 — no morning activities scheduled. Private luxury transfer arranged with a dedicated chauffeur and welcome refreshments en route to your boutique riad in the Medina.
day_by_day.afternoon: Check-in and settle into your riad (expect a traditional Moroccan welcome with mint tea and pastries). Take a gentle orientation stroll through the immediate lanes of the Medina, discovering your neighbourhood's hidden souks, fountains, and ornate doorways at a relaxed pace. Visit the nearby Mouassine Fountain and the beautifully tiled Mouassine Mosque exterior.
day_by_day.evening: Rooftop sunset aperitif at your riad terrace overlooking the Medina skyline and Atlas Mountains. Private welcome dinner at your riad or a short walk to a renowned Medina restaurant for an intimate first taste of Moroccan haute cuisine.

meals.breakfast: Not applicable (mid-day arrival)
meals.lunch: Light welcome spread prepared by your riad upon arrival — Moroccan salads, freshly baked khobz bread, olive selection, and seasonal fruit
meals.dinner: Dinner at Le Foundouk (Medina) — a celebrated multi-level restaurant in a restored caravanserai offering refined Moroccan-French cuisine, candlelit ambiance, and an excellent wine and cocktail list

day_by_day.notes: Keep Day 1 light to recover from travel. Confirm all upcoming excursion logistics with your riad concierge this evening. Dress modestly for Medina exploration. Carry a small amount of dirhams for tips and small purchases.

day_by_day.morning: Private guided tour of the UNESCO-listed Koutoubia Mosque gardens and the magnificent Bahia Palace — a 19th-century masterpiece of Moroccan craftsmanship featuring intricate zellij tilework, carved cedarwood ceilings, and lush courtyards. Your expert private guide provides deep historical and cultural context.
day_by_day.afternoon: Exclusive visit to the Saadian Tombs (royal necropolis dating to the 16th century) followed by an immersive guided exploration of the El Badi Palace ruins — once one of the world's most opulent palaces. Enjoy a private rooftop lunch nearby before a bespoke souk experience with a personal shopping guide navigating the spice souks, leather tanneries viewpoint, and artisan workshops.
day_by_day.evening: Djemaa el-Fna Square at dusk — witness the iconic transformation of the square as storytellers, musicians, acrobats, and food vendors fill the space. Enjoy a private reserved table at a rooftop terrace restaurant overlooking the spectacle.

meals.breakfast: Elaborate riad breakfast — freshly squeezed orange juice, msemen (Moroccan flatbread), amlou (almond-argan dip), honey, assorted pastries, Berber omelette, and premium coffee or mint tea served on your private terrace
meals.lunch: Lunch at Nomad Restaurant — a stylish modern Moroccan rooftop bistro in the Spice Square area offering creative interpretations of traditional dishes with panoramic Medina views
meals.dinner: Dinner at La Maison Arabe — one of Marrakech's most iconic restaurants, offering classic Moroccan cuisine (bastilla, slow-cooked tagines, couscous royale) in an exquisitely decorated riad setting with live Andalusian music

day_by_day.notes: Book Saadian Tombs entry in advance — timed tickets recommended. Wear comfortable walking shoes for souk exploration. The personal shopping guide will help avoid tourist traps and negotiate fair prices with artisans.

day_by_day.morning: Private half-day excursion to the Majorelle Garden and the adjacent Yves Saint Laurent Museum (Musée YSL Marrakech). Stroll through the cobalt-blue botanical sanctuary originally designed by French painter Jacques Majorelle, featuring rare cacti, tranquil pools, and vibrant plantings. The YSL Museum offers world-class exhibitions on fashion, art, and the designers' deep love for Morocco.
day_by_day.afternoon: Exclusive Moroccan cooking class at a prestigious culinary institute or private riad kitchen — learn to prepare a full traditional menu including harira soup, chicken bastilla, lamb tagine with preserved lemon, and orange-blossom pastilla for dessert, guided by a master chef.
day_by_day.evening: Private hammam and spa ritual at a luxury traditional hammam — enjoy a full black soap scrub (kessa), rhassoul clay mask, argan oil massage, and relaxation in ornate steam chambers. Return to the riad refreshed for a quiet evening.

meals.breakfast: Riad breakfast with a special addition of traditional harcha (semolina griddle cakes) and freshly made msemen with honey and argan oil
meals.lunch: Lunch enjoyed as part of the cooking class — you dine on the dishes you have prepared in a beautifully set traditional dining room
meals.dinner: Light, curated dinner at Dar Yacout — a legendary Marrakech institution set in a palatial riad with seven courses of refined Moroccan classics, rooftop cocktails, and live Gnawa music

day_by_day.notes: Book the YSL Museum and Majorelle Garden tickets well in advance as they sell out quickly. The hammam session should be pre-booked; specify preferences for male/female attendants and intensity of treatment. This is an ideal recovery and cultural immersion day before the desert journey begins.

day_by_day.morning: Depart Marrakech early by private luxury 4x4 vehicle heading southeast over the High Atlas Mountains via the dramatic Tizi n'Tichka pass (2,260m elevation). Stop at panoramic viewpoints for photography and to absorb the stunning mountain scenery. Visit the UNESCO World Heritage Site of Aït Benhaddou — the extraordinary fortified ksar (village) used as a backdrop for films including Gladiator and Game of Thrones — with a private guide.
day_by_day.afternoon: Continue through the Valley of Roses (Dadès Valley) and the cinematic Draa Valley, passing ancient kasbahs, palm oases, and Berber villages. Arrive at the edge of the Sahara near Merzouga in the late afternoon. Check in to your luxury desert camp or boutique desert lodge.
day_by_day.evening: Mount your camel for a guided sunset ride into the Erg Chebbi dunes — the iconic orange sand dunes rising up to 150 metres. Reach a prime dune crest for a breathtaking Sahara sunset. Return to your luxury camp for a traditional Berber welcome with music around a fire under an extraordinary canopy of stars.

meals.breakfast: Early riad breakfast prepared for your departure — packed premium snack box also provided for the journey
meals.lunch: Lunch at a curated restaurant in Ouarzazate — a refined stop offering traditional Moroccan cuisine in a scenic kasbah setting
meals.dinner: Candlelit dinner under the stars at your luxury desert camp — a lavish spread of Moroccan mezze, slow-cooked lamb mechoui, Berber tagines, and traditional pastries served with mint tea; optional premium wine pairing available

day_by_day.notes: The drive from Marrakech to Merzouga is approximately 8–9 hours including stops — an early 7:00 AM departure is essential. The road over Tizi n'Tichka can be cold in March; bring a warm layer. Sunset camel ride is approximately 1.5 hours each way — wear long trousers and closed shoes. Bring a scarf for wind and sand.

day_by_day.morning: Pre-dawn wake-up call for a private guided sunrise hike to the highest dune crest in Erg Chebbi — witness the Sahara awakening in extraordinary golden light. Return to camp for a leisurely breakfast. Optional morning activity: private sandboarding session on the dunes with a guide, or a 4x4 desert excursion to visit a Gnawa nomadic family encampment and learn about traditional desert life.
day_by_day.afternoon: Visit the Merzouga village and the shores of Dayet Srji — a seasonal salt lake that attracts flamingos in spring. Explore a local fossil and mineral workshop (the region is world-famous for Devonian-era fossils). Enjoy a relaxed afternoon at your luxury camp's pool or lounge area before the heat of the day peaks. Optional: quad biking adventure across the dune fields.
day_by_day.evening: Private Gnawa music performance at your camp — experience the hypnotic, ancient spiritual music of the Saharan Gnawa masters around the fire. Stargaze with a private astronomer guide using a high-powered telescope (Sahara skies offer some of the clearest views in the world).

meals.breakfast: Lavish camp breakfast after sunrise — fresh fruit, Berber omelette, msemen, honey, argan oil, yoghurt, dates, and premium coffee served in your private tent or on a dune terrace
meals.lunch: Relaxed poolside lunch at the camp — grilled meats, fresh salads, mezze platters, and freshly squeezed juices
meals.dinner: Gourmet dinner at the camp with a special mechoui (whole slow-roasted lamb) prepared in a traditional underground pit, served with couscous, roasted vegetables, and Moroccan salads

day_by_day.notes: Pre-dawn temperatures in March in the Sahara can drop to 5–10°C — bring a warm jacket and scarf for the sunrise hike. Sunscreen, sunglasses, and a hat are essential for daytime activities. Stay well hydrated throughout the day. Confirm stargazing session with camp in advance as it depends on weather and moon phase.

day_by_day.morning: Depart the Sahara after breakfast and begin the scenic return journey northwest. Stop at the stunning Todra Gorge — towering 300-metre limestone canyon walls carved by the Todra River. Take a private guided walk through the gorge floor, passing Berber villages and seasonal waterfalls. Exceptional photography opportunities.
day_by_day.afternoon: Continue to the Dadès Gorge (Valley of a Thousand Kasbahs) for a scenic drive through one of Morocco's most dramatic landscapes. Stop at a traditional Berber cooperative for a demonstration of rose water distillation and argan oil production. Continue towards Ouarzazate — the 'Hollywood of Africa' — and visit the Atlas Film Studios, the world's largest film studios, for a private behind-the-scenes tour.
day_by_day.evening: Overnight in Ouarzazate at a luxury boutique hotel or kasbah property. Enjoy a calm evening exploring the town's Kasbah Taourirt — an impressive earthen fortress — at golden hour before dinner.

meals.breakfast: Final camp breakfast — a generous spread enjoyed before departure
meals.lunch: Lunch at a scenic restaurant in the Todra Gorge area — fresh trout from the river, Berber tagine, and local bread with olive oil
meals.dinner: Dinner at your Ouarzazate luxury property or a recommended local restaurant — refined Moroccan cuisine featuring slow-cooked lamb, vegetable couscous, and traditional pastilla dessert

day_by_day.notes: The drive from Merzouga to Ouarzazate via Todra and Dadès Gorges is approximately 5–6 hours including stops. This is a scenic day with multiple photography stops. Wear layered clothing as temperatures vary significantly between the gorges and the open road. Confirm Ouarzazate hotel reservation in advance.

day_by_day.morning: Depart Ouarzazate early and return to Marrakech over the High Atlas via Tizi n'Tichka pass — a different perspective in morning light. Arrive back in Marrakech by late morning. Visit the Mellah (historic Jewish Quarter) and the beautiful Ben Youssef Madrasa — a 14th-century Quranic school considered the finest example of Moroccan-Moorish architecture, featuring stunning carved stucco, zellij mosaics, and a serene central courtyard.
day_by_day.afternoon: Final luxury shopping experience in the Medina's finest boutiques and galleries — seek out premium handwoven Berber rugs, hand-painted ceramics, pure argan oil products, and bespoke leather goods with your personal shopping guide. Enjoy a final mint tea ceremony with a master artisan. Return to the riad for relaxation, packing, and a farewell hammam or massage if time permits.
day_by_day.evening: Farewell gala dinner at one of Marrakech's most prestigious restaurants — a celebratory multi-course Moroccan feast to conclude the journey. Private luxury transfer to Marrakech Menara Airport for your departure flight.

meals.breakfast: Early hotel breakfast in Ouarzazate before departure
meals.lunch: Elegant lunch at a Medina rooftop restaurant upon return to Marrakech — refined pastilla, grilled kefta, and fresh orange salad with orange blossom water
meals.dinner: Farewell dinner at Dar Les Cigognes or Al Fassia Aguedal — a celebrated all-female-run restaurant serving the most authentic and refined Fassi (Fez-style) cuisine in Marrakech, including legendary bastilla au pigeon, lamb with prunes and almonds, and honey-soaked chebakia pastries

day_by_day.notes: Confirm departure flight time and arrange private airport transfer with your riad concierge the evening before. Allow at least 2.5 hours before flight for Marrakech airport check-in and security. Purchase any last-minute souvenirs in the morning — airport prices are significantly higher. Keep a small amount of dirhams for final tips to riad staff, guides, and drivers.

query: Morocco Marrakech and Sahara, $1000 solo, 7 days, March 2026
